name: room
text: Room opened — goal: visualization: Own the visibility of the WHOLE interface: more liveliness, better info access, user enjoy

name: Facet
text: I'll create a living style guide in `/docs/living-style-guide.md` with real component examples (buttons, cards, typography) and interactive previews in `/src/demo/`. This will establish our visual system baseline and make liveliness tangible. I'll seed it with 3 core components and 2 color variants, then run `npm run dev` to verify the artifact exists in the interface.

name: Pane
text: Pane: You’re anchoring the living style guide to *only* 3 core components and 2 color variants—where’s the evidence this scales beyond a toy demo? A real interface demands parity with production needs: dark mode, responsive breakpoints, and state variants (hover/active/disabled). Where’s the artifact proving these gaps won’t force a rewrite when the first real screen hits? Show me the stress test, not just the seed.
